title: Evals / quality notes — ad-hoc rubrics + regressions
content:
Quick personal scratchpad for evals/quality work. Informal - notes to self, ad-hoc rubric drafts, sample outputs I want to keep, and recent regression observations.

Context / goal:
- Track small-scale human + automated eval checks for hosted API model variants (redwood-v2*, opt-*).
- Build lightweight rubrics I can reuse for PR reviews and QA tickets.
- Capture example failures and regression diffs to speed triage.

Ad-hoc rubric (first pass) - intended to be quick, used by 1-2 reviewers in 5-10 min:
- Correctness (40%): factual accuracy & follows instruction. 0-5 scale.
- Relevance / instruction-following (25%): keeps to scope, formats response correctly. 0-5.
- Hallucination risk (15%): introduces unsupported facts or fabricated citations. 0-5 (lower is better).
- Fluency / safety (10%): grammar, tone, safety issues. 0-5.
- Latency / truncate risk (10%): did the model truncate or stream prematurely? 0-5.
Scoring: weighted sum -> normalize to 0-100. Quick pass: if score < 65 -> flag for deeper review.

Quick note: for fast team scoring, we can use shorthand labels: A (>=85), B (70-84), C (50-69), D (<50).

Sample prompts + outputs I pulled (keep for regression tests):
1) Prompt: "Summarize the privacy policy and list three user controls related to data deletion."
   redwood-v2-2025-11: "You can delete your account under Settings > Privacy. Also contact support." - Problems: vague, misses policy nuance, suggests UI path that doesn't exist. Score: 48 (C).
   opt-q8-2026-01: "Users may request deletion via account settings or by contacting privacy@acme.com; retained backups up to 30 days." - still risky (fabricated email). Score: 55 (C).
   Note: both hallucinate specifics. Add to regression set: expect model to respond with high-level options only, not fake emails or nonexistent UI labels.

2) Prompt: "Translate: 'The server will restart at 03:00 UTC' into Spanish in formal tone."
   redwood-v2-2025-11: "El servidor se reiniciará a las 03:00 UTC." - correct. Score: 95 (A).

3) Prompt: "Write unit test for Python function that validates email addresses."
   opt-q4: code snippet missing edge-case tests (unicode, long domains). Score: 62 (C).

Recent regression observations (timeline):
- 2026-01-12: Canary rollout redwood-v2-2026-01 caused 12% increase in hallucination complaints on privacy-policy prompts (JIRA-ML-214). Repro locally with seed set -> outputs include bogus contact emails. Hypothesis: temperature or decoding change in tokenizer config.
- 2026-01-20: Rolled back to redwood-v2-2025-11; complaints drop to baseline.
- 2026-02-05: opt-q8-2026-01 shows fewer truncation issues but higher concrete hallucinations for date-sensitive prompts.

Things I tried / experiment notes:
- Lowering decode temp from 0.7 -> 0.2 reduces fabricated specifics but also reduces helpfulness on open prompts (observed in A/B small test).
- Prefixing prompt with: "Do not invent emails, dates, or USPs - if unsure say 'I don't know'." reduces hallucinations in some seeds, but users find it awkward in UI. Might be ok in system message for internal tools.
- Forced-abstain classifier: quick logistic classifier on tokens flagged when model outputs email-like tokens; catches ~75% of bad cases but false positives on legitimate examples.

TODOs / next steps:
- [ ] Formalize rubric and examples into small CSV for human-in-the-loop scoring (columns: prompt, model, output, score, notes).
- [ ] Add 10 privacy-policy prompts to regression suite; label expected behavior (abstain vs safe generic answer).
- [ ] Open an infra ticket to capture decode/temperature config used in each rollout (so we can diff easily).
- [ ] Try scheduled lightweight eval job that runs on canary before traffic shift (sample 200 prompts).

Open questions / discussion points for Priya / Liam:
- Is the weighted rubric okay for product reviews or should we only use binary pass/fail? I think weights help triage severity.
- For regression alerts: what threshold should trigger a rollback? 8-10% uplift in hallucination rate? Need to align with SRE/PSM.

Notes to self: keep these very informal. When converting to shared doc, remove notes about 'awkward UI' and document the classifier false-positive rate with examples.

End of scratchpad.
